summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=review) for the accepted direct check c30f6cc0db39422ab3985999ab44c9a7 (version 1) of obligation c-reported-configuration-index, the fifth defect and the last one still awaiting attribution. No input issue is open on this artifact, so the submission carries only the required checker_correspondence item, which reviews the requirement, the encoded predicate, the fixed inputs, the binding, the oracle, the correlated observations, the legality and the counterevidence together. The item (no_issue_found, 6 cited ranges, 5 retained limitations) states the obligation — the configuration future returned by Raft.GetConfiguration must report the log index at which the configuration it returns was established, so a caller can relate the participant set it receives to a log position and to the value the library publishes for the same future — and shows how the check encodes it: the entry point is the accessor that builds its future from the copy of the latest configuration and never sets that value's index field while the same field is documented as the index of the applied entry and published as latest_configuration_index in Stats; the fixed inputs are the package's own NewRaft and BootstrapCluster on a single-voter configuration, so the configuration entry is the only log entry and its index is the log's last index; only public accessors are used and no target file is modified; the binding locates the accessor; applicability requires the returned configuration to still contain the local voter so a stale or empty configuration cannot be mistaken for an index defect; and the admission event precedes the result in the single runner stream with matching identity. The retained observation is the violation: configuration_established with index 1 and log_last_index 1, then configuration_index_observed with reported_index 0, stats_index "0", configuration_has_self true, log_last_index 1 and state Follower, at exit 0. Counterevidence is kept explicit: the returned Configuration value itself is correct and current, so callers ignoring the index are unaffected; the index exists inside the main goroutine and is omitted rather than unavailable; nothing documents that it may be unset while it is published as a metric; and no other public accessor offers the pair. The limitations record that the prefix holds a single configuration entry so the comparison cannot distinguish an always-wrong index from a first-configuration-only difference, that the check observes a value rather than a state transition with no downstream consequence measured, that no consumer dependency was established, that the configuration is only checked for containing the local voter, and that the repair location remains open. With the only blocker answered, the assessment for this artifact should recompute to a confirmed violated comparison at implementation_obligation level, completing the obligation and turning its conclusion into a confirmed in-scope result, which would leave the run with five confirmed findings (three consensus-safety, one bounded-liveness, one implementation-semantics) and the remaining frontier limited to the productions-TCP scheduling question, the enqueue-before-shutdown question, the configuration-change/matching question and one deferred surface about the commit context a follower leaves after installing a snapshot. Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; the review introduces no new execution and no map change, and the two Chinese fields are presentation only.
